description: The information systems, data models and governance that turn clinical trials, health records, registries and biobanks into evidence. Students design trial databases, map routine data into a common data model, define patient cohorts in SQL, link records, and weigh privacy decisions in realistic cases.
modelledOn: Richesson and Andrews, Clinical Research Informatics
Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics, The Book of OHDSI
ICH E6 Good Clinical Practice guideline and CDISC standards documentation
Hernan and Robins, Causal Inference: What If
outcomes: Design the data capture, validation and standards pipeline for a clinical trial.
Transform routine health data into a common data model and assess its quality and fitness for a research question.
Define and validate computable phenotypes and cohorts from structured data and clinical text.
Build warehouse and lake structures for health data, and link records across sources while measuring linkage error.
Apply de-identification, differential privacy and federated analysis, and judge consent and governance arrangements.
Plan an observational study from question to analysis plan, naming its main biases.

units.title: Clinical trial data management
topics: Trial phases and designs: parallel, cluster and stepped-wedge randomised trials
Protocols, eligibility criteria and case report form design
Electronic data capture, data dictionaries and edit checks
CDISC standards: CDASH, SDTM and ADaM datasets
Data cleaning, query management, audit trails and Good Clinical Practice
Randomisation, blinding and safety reporting systems

units.title: Observational databases and common data models
topics: Observational designs: cohort, case-control and self-controlled studies
Bias and confounding: selection, information bias and confounding by indication
The OMOP common data model: person, visit, condition, drug and measurement tables
Extract-transform-load into a common data model; vocabulary mapping (ICD-10, SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm)
Data quality assessment: completeness, plausibility and conformance checks
Distributed research networks and federated queries

units.title: Cohort discovery and phenotyping
topics: Cohort definitions: inclusion, exclusion, index date and observation windows
Rule-based computable phenotypes from diagnoses, labs and drugs
Machine-learning phenotyping and weak labels
Clinical text mining: concept extraction, negation and temporality
Phenotype validation: chart review, sensitivity and positive predictive value
Temporal and sequence phenotypes; disease progression patterns

units.title: Electronic health record data re-use
topics: What a record contains and what it omits: coverage, coding practice and workflow effects
Missing data and informative observation
Longitudinal events, time series and irregular sampling
Linking diagnoses, laboratory results and medicines across tables
Secondary use and the learning health system
Routine facility data in low-resource settings: completeness and timeliness

units.title: Data warehouses and data lakes for health
topics: Star schema design for clinical data: facts, dimensions and slowly changing attributes
Warehouse, data lake and lakehouse compared
ETL and ELT pipelines, lineage and provenance
Query performance: indexes, partitions and materialised views
FHIR bulk export and bridging between standards and analytic tables
Data catalogues, metadata and the FAIR principles

units.title: Registries, biobanks and linkage
topics: Disease registries: design, case ascertainment and completeness
Biobanks: consent, sample metadata and access
Record linkage: deterministic matching and probabilistic match weights
Linkage error and its effect on bias
Linking clinical and genomic data

units.title: Privacy-preserving analysis and data governance
topics: De-identification: identifiers, safe-harbour style removal, expert determination and k-anonymity
Differential privacy: sensitivity, the Laplace mechanism and the privacy budget
Federated learning and secure multiparty computation for health data
Consent models: broad, dynamic and opt-out; data sharing agreements
Ghana Data Protection Act and cross-border transfer of health data
Trusted research environments and data access committees

units.title: From question to study
topics: Turning a clinical question into an analysis plan on real-world data
Target trial emulation
Reporting standards for observational studies
Capstone: design and critique a real-world data study

schedule.title: Trial designs, protocols and case report forms
schedule.exercise: Draft a short protocol for a cluster-randomised trial of malaria bed nets, list eligibility rules, and design a one-page case report form with a data dictionary.

tasks.title: Design tables for a trial case report form with patients, visits and measurements, and add keys and types for each field
Write 10 edit-check queries over a trial table that flag out-of-range vitals, missing visits and visit dates before enrolment
Compute the sample size for a cluster trial with an intracluster correlation of 0.05 and compare it with an individually randomised trial

schedule.title: CDISC standards, cleaning and safety
schedule.exercise: Map six case report form fields to SDTM variables, and describe how an audit trail would show who changed a lab value and why.

tasks.title: Map a raw adverse-event table to SDTM-style columns with SQL, renaming fields and coding the severity values as the standard requires
Generate a permuted-block randomisation list for 120 participants in 3 sites with 1:1 allocation and verify balance within each block
Handle a trial in a case where a site backdated a visit, reviewing audit trail evidence, choosing corrective action and scoring the effect on data integrity

schedule.title: Observational designs, bias and the common data model
schedule.exercise: Describe the cohort and case-control designs for a study of a new antimalarial in pregnancy, and name the main bias in each.

tasks.title: Draw the person, visit, condition and drug tables of a common data model and write a query counting persons with a condition
Compute risk ratio and odds ratio with confidence intervals from a 2x2 table in a cohort and a case-control design, and explain why they differ
Simulate confounding by indication in a drug study, show the crude and adjusted effect estimates, and report how strongly the bias depends on severity

schedule.title: ETL, data quality and federated queries
schedule.exercise: Write the mapping specification from a local hospital diagnosis table to standard vocabulary, with rules for unmapped codes and duplicates.

tasks.title: Map local diagnosis codes to standard concepts using a vocabulary table and report the share of rows left unmapped
Write data quality checks for completeness, plausibility and conformance on a drug exposure table, and summarise failing rows by rule
Run the same cohort count at three simulated sites, share only aggregate counts, and combine them while suppressing cells below five

schedule.title: Cohort definitions and rule-based phenotypes
schedule.exercise: Write a computable phenotype for type 2 diabetes from diagnoses, HbA1c results and medicines, and describe how each rule could mislabel a patient.

tasks.title: Write SQL for a cohort of adults with a first hypertension diagnosis and at least 365 days of prior observation, and report the count
Build a diabetes phenotype from diagnoses, lab values and medicine records, and show how the cohort size changes as each rule is added
Train a classifier for a phenotype from weak labels created by the rule-based definition, and compare its predictions with the rules on 200 records

schedule.title: Text mining, validation and temporal patterns
schedule.exercise: Compute sensitivity and positive predictive value for a phenotype from a chart review of 100 records, and explain how a negated phrase can fool a keyword search.

tasks.title: Compute sensitivity, specificity and positive predictive value of a phenotype against a chart-review gold standard of 100 records
Extract symptom mentions from 50 clinical notes with rules, handle negation and history phrases, and measure the error against labels
Find patients whose first diagnosis, drug start and lab abnormality occur in a given order within 180 days, and count the pattern by age group

schedule.title: Record re-use, missingness and routine data
schedule.exercise: List three ways a health record can misrepresent the true patient population, and say how each would bias an estimate of disease prevalence.

tasks.title: Summarise missingness per variable in a 5000-row record extract, plot the pattern, and judge if values are missing at random
Join diagnoses, laboratory results and prescriptions for 1000 patients, then compute the time from first abnormal lab to first prescription
Judge in a case whether district routine data are good enough to estimate antenatal coverage, weighing completeness, timeliness and duplicate reports

schedule.title: Warehouse design and the lake
schedule.exercise: Draw a star schema for hospital admissions with fact and dimension tables, and compare when a warehouse or a data lake suits a dataset of images and notes.

tasks.title: Create a star schema for admissions with patient, diagnosis, ward and date dimensions, and load a small dataset into it
Write 5 analytic queries on the admissions star schema, including admissions per ward per month and average stay by diagnosis
Build an extract-transform-load script with a lineage log for three source tables, and rerun it to show it is repeatable and idempotent

schedule.title: Performance, standards bridges and metadata
schedule.exercise: Explain how an index and a partition would speed up a query for all laboratory results in one month, and list the metadata a catalogue entry needs.

tasks.title: Read the query plan of a lab-results query on a million rows, add an index, and compare the plans and timings
Flatten a bulk export of Patient and Observation resources into analytic tables, and check the row counts against the source
Prepare a dataset for sharing in a case, writing catalogue metadata and a data dictionary, and score findability, access, interoperability and reuse

schedule.title: Registries, biobanks and record linkage
schedule.exercise: Estimate the completeness of a cancer registry with two overlapping sources, and design match rules for linking records where names are spelt differently.

tasks.title: Link two patient tables by exact match on name and date of birth, then count matched, unmatched and ambiguous records
Implement probabilistic linkage with string similarity and match weights for 500 record pairs, and choose thresholds for match, review and non-match
Measure precision and recall of a linkage on a known truth set, then show how missed links bias a mortality estimate

schedule.title: De-identification and differential privacy
schedule.exercise: Find the quasi-identifiers in a small clinic dataset, generalise them to reach k = 5, and explain what the privacy budget epsilon controls.

tasks.title: Check k-anonymity of a clinic table on age, sex and postcode, and list the groups smaller than five records
Release a patient count with the Laplace mechanism at three epsilon values over 1000 repeats, and plot the error against epsilon
Fit a logistic model with federated averaging across 4 simulated hospitals, and compare accuracy with a pooled model and a single-site model

schedule.title: Consent, law and access governance
schedule.exercise: Draft the key clauses of a data sharing agreement for a hospital sharing records with a research group, covering purpose, security, onward sharing and return of data.

tasks.title: Decide in a case whether a clinic may share patient data with a researcher, citing the data protection rules and consent given
Choose broad or dynamic consent for a new biobank in a case, weighing participant trust, rural access and the cost of re-contact
Sit on a data access committee in a case, assess three requests for linked health data, and approve, limit or refuse each with reasons

schedule.title: Real-world data study design
schedule.exercise: Write the analysis plan for a real-world study of two blood pressure drugs, stating the target trial, cohort, outcome, confounders and sensitivity analyses.

tasks.title: Check a draft observational study report against a reporting checklist in a case, and list the missing items with the risk each creates
Specify the eligibility, treatment strategies, time zero and follow-up of a target trial, then build the matching cohort tables in SQL
Run a full real-world analysis on a synthetic records dataset, adjust for confounders, test sensitivity to an unmeasured one, and write the methods and limitations
